reasons: The rule's preferred position is that no non-solicit bind the Customer; absence of any solicitation/no-hire covenant therefore maps to 'compliant' rather than 'missing', since the omission favors our party.

The cited § 14.8 Personnel text addresses only each party's supervision of its own personnel, IBM's assignment rights, and subcontracting — it contains no 'shall not solicit', 'employ or engage', 'no-hire' or inducement language, so the rationale is consistent with the quoted paragraphs.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was proposed and no counterparty comment was generated; the redline output is byte-identical to the original paragraphs.

The failing deterministic sub-checks (12-month duration, general-solicitation carve-out) are correctly treated as vacuous: there is no covenant whose duration or carve-outs could be measured, so their failure does not undercut compliance.

The rationale appropriately preserves the fallback position as internal negotiation guidance without raising it as an issue, matching the playbook's treatment of compliant findings as evaluation evidence only.
